_why: TWO NUMBERS PER RESOURCE, AND THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THEM IS THE WHOLE POLICY.
`resources` is the SPEND TARGET. A run that stays inside it was efficient and that is
still what every run should try to do. Reducing spend is a real goal and these numbers
are deliberately tight.
`escalation_ceiling` is the HARD STOP. Between the two, the controller GRANTS the work,
records a `budget_escalated` event naming the resource and the overage, and carries on.
It does not refuse, and it does not push the run toward a terminal needs_review.
WHY IT WORKS THIS WAY, owner's decision on 2026-08-28: AN EMPTY RUN IS WORSE THAN AN
EXPENSIVE ONE. The definition of done is a DELIVERED VIDEO. On that day the August 28th
Dispatch reached a panel mean of 6.986 against a 7.0 bar, a gap of fourteen thousandths,
with a playable film and three judges reporting no hard fails, and it stopped, because
renders and animatics had run out. Every prescribed fix was known, specific and cheap.
The machine had the answers and no allowance left to apply them, so it wrote up a
failure instead of a film.
That is the wrong trade and it was the cost model making an editorial decision it has no
standing to make. A cap that turns a nearly-finished film into no film has not saved
money, it has spent the whole day's research, fact-check, voice and render budget and
thrown away the only thing that was for.
One render lost to a tooling defect that day, a wait loop matching its own command line,
took twenty percent of the render budget without producing a frame. Under the old caps
that single bug was enough to decide the run's terminal state. Under escalation it is a
line in the ledger.
WHAT ESCALATION IS NOT. It is not permission to iterate forever, and it is not a way past
a QUALITY gate. The rubric bar, every rubric hard fail, the numeral-traces-to-a-fetched-
quote rule, the ban on time-stretching and the alignment evidence are untouched by any of
this and are not escalatable. Escalation buys a run more ATTEMPTS at clearing the bar. It
never lowers the bar, and `bar_check.py` still proves the threshold is stated once.

BOARD FORMAT, max_runtime_s 55 -> 62 on 2026-08-28: Raised from 55 to 62 on 2026-08-28, owner directed. This is a FORMAT band, not a truth guard, and it was forcing a real choice the wrong way: the corrected read came back at 56.7s and the only ways under 55 were to gamble another synthesis on a shorter delivery or to cut a line that carries evidence. Neither improves the film. The band exists so a Dispatch stays feed-sized, and a few seconds does not change that. Nothing here touches the rubric, the hard fails or the evidence rules, which are the guards that make the product worth watching.
